headline_marked: [[Shoriful Islam sets new Bangladesh bowling record]] in away Test, takes 7 wickets against Australia
headline: Shoriful Islam sets new Bangladesh bowling record in away Test, takes 7 wickets against Australia
summary: Pacer Shoriful Islam achieved the best bowling figures by a Bangladeshi in an away Test, taking 7 wickets for 48 runs against Australia on Day 2 in Mackay. Despite his heroics, Australia secured a 146-run first-innings lead.
details: Pacer Shoriful Islam recorded the best bowling figures by a Bangladeshi in an away Test, claiming seven wickets for 48 runs against Australia. This remarkable performance occurred on Day 2 of the second and final Test at the Great Barrier Reef Arena in Mackay.
Australia was eventually bundled out for 210 in 52.3 overs, having resumed their innings at 165 for eight. Shoriful's crucial dismissal of Cameron Green, who scored a team-high 67, was a highlight.
Green was removed by a scintillating inswinging yorker that struck him on the toe, confirmed after a DRS review. This ended a 38-run ninth-wicket stand with Nathan Lyon.

Shoriful's seven for 48 surpassed Shahadat Hossain's six for 27 against South Africa in Mirpur in 2008, making it the best by a Bangladesh quick in Tests. It also beat Taijul Islam's seven for 138 against Zimbabwe earlier this year for best away Test figures.
Despite Shoriful's career-best efforts, Australia managed to extend their lead. Nathan Lyon remained unbeaten on 32, contributing to a 24-run final-wicket stand with Josh Hazlewood.
Ultimately, Australia secured a substantial 146-run first-innings lead, setting up a challenging task for the Tigers in the remainder of the match.
caption:
Bangladesh's Shoriful Islam made history with the best bowling figures by a Bangladeshi in an away Test!

Pacer Shoriful Islam recorded the best bowling figures by a Bangladeshi in an away Test, claiming seven wickets for 48 runs against Australia. This remarkable performance occurred on Day 2 of the second and final Test at the Great Barrier Reef Arena in Mackay.

Australia was eventually bundled out for 210 in 52.3 overs, having resumed their innings at 165 for eight. Shoriful's crucial dismissal of Cameron Green, who scored a team-high 67, was a highlight.

Green was removed by a scintillating inswinging yorker that struck him on the toe, confirmed after a DRS review. This ended a 38-run ninth-wicket stand with Nathan Lyon.

Shoriful's seven for 48 surpassed Shahadat Hossain's six for 27 against South Africa in Mirpur in 2008, making it the best by a Bangladesh quick in Tests. It also beat Taijul Islam's seven for 138 against Zimbabwe earlier this year for best away Test figures.

Despite Shoriful's career-best efforts, Australia managed to extend their lead. Nathan Lyon remained unbeaten on 32, contributing to a 24-run final-wicket stand with Josh Hazlewood.

Ultimately, Australia secured a substantial 146-run first-innings lead, setting up a challenging task for the Tigers in the remainder of the match.

headline: Four bodies recovered from locked house in Rangpur; police launch murder investigation
summary: Police found the bodies of a former school teacher, his wife, daughter, and son after locals reported a foul smell from their locked home. A CID team is investigating the cause of death.
details: Police have recovered the bodies of four members of the same family, including a former Zilla School teacher, from their locked home in Masuapara, Rangpur Metropolitan area. The grim discovery was made on Saturday night (August 22) after police broke the lock.

The deceased have been identified as Ganapati Chakraborty (65), his wife Pritilata Chakraborty (50), daughter Prarthi Chakraborty (25), and son Ayush Chakraborty (12). The family had reportedly been living in the house for some time.

Local residents informed the police after noticing the house's main gate had been locked for several days and a foul odor was emanating from inside. Upon arrival, police broke the lock to enter the premises, where they found the four bodies.

A special CID team is currently at the scene, collecting necessary evidence. The officer-in-charge of Rangpur Metropolitan Kotwali Police Station, Nazmul Kader, confirmed the incident and stated that an investigation has begun to determine the cause and circumstances of the deaths.

The bodies will be sent to Rangpur Medical College Hospital for a post-mortem examination to prepare a preliminary report. Police are treating the incident with the utmost seriousness, aiming to uncover how and why this tragedy occurred.
